note: The surf spots and place names on the Surf forecast map. Edit by hand. 'faces' is the compass bearing the beach looks out on, in degrees (270 = due west); the score uses it to tell how squarely the swell arrives and whether the wind is offshore. The wave forecast is read 3 km out to sea in that direction; 'seaKm' changes the distance where an island is in the way.

spots.name: Poppit Sands
spots.about: Sheltered estuary-mouth beach. Needs a big swell; gentle when it works.

spots.name: Newport Sands
spots.about: Wide north-facing bay. Small and mellow unless the swell is large.

spots.name: Abermawr
spots.about: Quiet north-coast cove that picks up westerly swell.

spots.name: Abereiddy
spots.about: Dark-sand bay with reef either side. Better for experienced surfers.

spots.name: Whitesands
spots.about: The best-known beach near St Davids. Busy, with room for learners in the middle.

spots.name: Newgale
spots.about: Two miles of sand open to the Atlantic. Something for every level.

spots.name: Broad Haven
spots.about: Smaller and gentler than Newgale, tucked into St Brides Bay.

spots.name: Marloes Sands
spots.about: Remote south-west-facing beach with rocks. A walk in, and no lifeguards.

spots.name: West Dale
spots.about: Compact bay that catches plenty of swell, with strong currents.

spots.name: Freshwater West
spots.about: The most consistent surf in Wales. Powerful, with strong rips.

spots.name: Broad Haven South
spots.about: South-facing cove near Bosherston. Works when the west coast is too big.

spots.name: Manorbier
spots.about: Castle-backed bay with a right-hand reef point. Needs a solid swell.

spots.name: Freshwater East
spots.about: Sheltered south-east-facing bay. A stormy-day option.

spots.name: Tenby South Beach
spots.about: Long sheltered beach. Only breaks in the biggest swells.
